categories.main_business_segments: Pure Storage operates as a single reportable segment focused on data management and storage solutions. Its primary offerings include integrated hardware and software storage products (FlashArray and FlashBlade families), cloud-native storage solutions (Portworx), and a portfolio of subscription-based services (Evergreen suite).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies are built around all-flash storage systems, leveraging proprietary Purity Operating Software, DirectFlash hardware modules, and advanced flash management capabilities. Manufacturing is outsourced to contract manufacturers, with Pure Storage providing specifications and quality oversight. The company emphasizes deep integration of hardware and software, enabling non-disruptive upgrades and high efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Pure Storage serves over 13,500 customers globally, including large enterprises, hyperscalers (notably Meta), managed service providers, and organizations across various industries. Its solutions address mission-critical workloads, analytics, AI/ML, backup, disaster recovery, and cloud-native applications, with a significant presence in approximately 62% of Fortune 500 companies.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates worldwide, with the majority of revenue generated in the United States and significant operations in EMEA, APAC, and the Americas. It maintains offices and R&D centers in North America, Europe, India, and other regions, and sells through both direct and channel partner networks globally.
categories.supply_chain_position: Pure Storage is positioned downstream in the supply chain, delivering finished data storage systems and services directly to end customers and through channel partners. It relies on upstream suppliers for components and contract manufacturers for assembly, while focusing on product design, integration, and customer support.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding all-flash storage into new use cases (replacing disk), enabling hybrid cloud architectures, growing subscription and as-a-Service offerings, and advancing AI/HPC storage solutions. R&D is focused on increasing flash density, software innovation, sustainability, and supporting hyperscaler and AI workloads.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through a mix of product sales (hardware and embedded software), recurring subscription services (Evergreen suite, Portworx, Cloud Block Store), and professional services. Subscription services are recognized over contract periods, while product revenue is recognized upon delivery or commencement of service.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include legacy storage vendors (Dell EMC, NetApp, Hitachi Vantara, HPE, IBM), public cloud providers, and hyperconverged infrastructure vendors. Pure Storage differentiates itself through technology innovation, simplicity, and customer experience, and continues to gain market share despite competitors’ larger scale and resources.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2025, Pure Storage reported $3.17 billion in total revenue, representing 12% year-over-year growth. Subscription annual recurring revenue grew 21% to $1.66 billion. The company is profitable, with net income of $106.7 million, and maintains a strong balance sheet with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Pure Storage emphasizes unmatched simplicity, reliability (99.9999% uptime), and efficiency, with a cloud-like operating model and non-disruptive upgrades. Its all-flash architecture delivers superior performance, lower total cost of ownership, and sustainability benefits, while its subscription model and customer-centric culture drive high loyalty and Net Promoter Scores.
